title: Grateful Dead Live at Trouper's Hall on 1966-03-25

ai_review.summary: Clear early‑'66 matrix recording that captures a classic Pigpen‑driven show with thunderous organ and standouts like “Hog For You” and “Hey Little One”.
ai_review.review: The tape offers surprisingly crisp separation of vocals and instruments for a 1966 live capture, though the organ can dominate the mix and the kick drum distorts in places. Musically it’s a quintessential early Dead set – blues‑rock heavy, highlighted by Pigpen’s organ wizardry on “Hog For You”, “Hey Little One” and “You Don't Have to Ask”, with Jerry’s fiery guitar and solid vocal work. Overall listeners rave about the historic vibe despite occasional mix quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of 25 reviews rate the release 4‑5 stars, praising both performance and sound quality; only one low‑rating outlier and a single 2‑star comment do not shift the overall high average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clear split‑channel recording (vocals on one side, instruments on the other); organ is unusually loud and sometimes mutes vocals; kick drum distortion noted but disappears when summed to mono; overall listenable with occasional mix imbalance.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid early‑Dead R&B/rock set that flows naturally, showcasing Pigpen’s organ dominance and the band's raw energy; despite a few mix issues the performance feels cohesive and historically exciting.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar sometimes out of tune but compensates with passionate singing and fiery riffs.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is audible though slightly recessed in the mix, still solid throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is thunderous, often too high in the mix but a major highlight of the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Kick drum distortion noted on “Next Time You See Me”, otherwise drums drive the set.
